_comment: BUG-002, new standard mechanism (2026-10-07): tests Core1Runner's deadline-anchored pacing (the 'fixed_schedule' name and its sleep-after-work-pad alternative were retired 2026-10-09 - core1_fixed_schedule now only accepts true, see scenario.py), verified against Betaflight's own source as the architecturally correct fix for the retuning fragility the old pad-based mode kept hitting (Betaflight's scheduler.c: nextTargetCycles = lastTargetCycles + desiredPeriodCycles, immune to per-call cost as long as cost < period - see Core1Runner's own docstring for the current citation). core1_interval_us=1045 here is the ABSOLUTE PERIOD TARGET, not a pad - this matched a sleep-after-work pad's own original tuning from before the pad-based mode was retired (historical context only, not reproducible - the pad-based scenario files that produced it are gone). Unlike a sleep-after-work pad, this should not need re-tuning if update()'s own cost changes again - that is exactly the property being tested. Run interleaved and rotated against bins_off (natural/unpaced cadence, no core1_interval_us set - confirmed as the unpaced generalization check in BUG-002's post-fix validation) and two_channel_arming_check_300 (a different DShot speed), not in a block, to compare mechanisms. bins_off's own class-bin diagnostic field is separately retired and now a no-op - see its own file's comment - but that doesn't affect its role here as the unpaced comparison.
